pages.text: The red headscarf hung on the peg by the pillow. From the loft stairs, Mom said, "Coco, shall you put it on yourself today?" Coco clenched both front paws and looked up at the peg. "Me! I'll do it myself!"

Coco placed the scarf on their head and twisted the two ends around and around. Oh? It slipped loose and fell over their eyes. Everything went dark. "I can't see!" Holding the cloth, Coco twisted from side to side.
At last Coco pulled it off. Their mouth drooped, and both ears fell sideways. "I can't even tie my scarf..." Coco had wanted to do it alone, but the scarf wouldn't cooperate. It felt upsetting.
Mom sat beside Coco and untied her apron strings to show them. "This isn't a hard knot. It's two tails saying hello. Watch." Coco brought the two scarf ends under their chin too.
"One, both ends to the front! Two, cross them once!" Mom crossed her strings once. Coco did too. The two tails hugged each other. "Three, pull tight!" Coco pulled the knot with both paws.
The scarf stayed snug on Coco's head. Mom sang, "Headscarf on—knot pulled tight!" Coco shook their head and hopped about. It didn't fall off!
Coco touched the knot with a front paw. It stayed firmly in place. "Headscarf on—knot pulled tight!" Coco sang too. Mom retied her apron. "Mom's too—tight!"
Coco pattered downstairs. In the kitchen was Mr. Pig, who carried flour sacks. "Who tied your scarf today?" "Me!" Coco pulled the knot with both paws to show him. He grinned wide.
Now Coco knew three steps. "One, both ends to the front! Two, cross them once! Three, pull tight!" The next morning, Coco tied it alone, without Mom. "Headscarf on—knot pulled tight!" Coco called.

Mom lifted Coco high and pressed her cheek to Coco's. "Our bakery child can tie a scarf alone now!" Even a hard knot can be tied one step at a time. "Headscarf on—knot pulled tight! Tomorrow I'll do it too!" Coco smiled.
